clusters.label: p-Type thermoelectric behavior
clusters.definition: Positive-polarity ionic thermoelectric response to a temperature gradient.
clusters.reason: All describe p-type ionic thermoelectric behavior; electrode, hydrogel composition, and transport pathways remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Soret effect
clusters.definition: Temperature-gradient-driven redistribution of ions through thermal diffusion.
clusters.reason: The evidence consistently identifies the same thermal-diffusion mechanism. Different consequences, model conditions, and its reported elimination in one device do not change the concept.

clusters.label: Body-heat harvesting
clusters.definition: Recovery of thermal energy from the body to provide electrical energy.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same energy-harvesting application, despite different devices and assigned roles.

clusters.label: Hydrogen bonding
clusters.definition: An interaction involving a hydrogen donor and an acceptor site.
clusters.reason: All explicitly denote hydrogen bonding as an interaction class. Its partners, effects, and hypothesized versus asserted occurrence remain attached to the individual claims.

clusters.label: Thermopower (ionic)
clusters.definition: Thermally induced voltage per temperature difference associated with ionic transport or redistribution.
clusters.reason: The evidence identifies ionic thermoelectric response, including host-ion diffusion, living-leaf ionic response, and regulated hydrogel ion transport. Redox doping in m05519 is linked explicitly to host-ion redistribution.

clusters.label: Thermopower (electronic)
clusters.definition: Seebeck response associated with electronic charge carriers, expressed as thermally induced voltage per temperature difference.
clusters.reason: These semiconductor, oxide, skutterudite, and cuprate contexts concern electronic thermopower. Different compositions, carrier mechanisms, and increases or decreases describe claims about the same quantity, rather than distinct quantities.

unresolved.reason: The paper concerns mixed electronic-ionic conduction, and the supplied symmetry statement does not resolve whether thermopower denotes an electronic, ionic, or combined response.

clusters.label: Output power
clusters.definition: Electrical energy delivered per unit time by the energy-conversion system.
clusters.reason: All denote electrical output power; differences in materials, driving gradients, and concentration dependence do not redefine this quantity.

clusters.label: PVA hydrogel
clusters.definition: A hydrogel based on poly(vinyl alcohol).
clusters.reason: Both labels explicitly denote the PVA hydrogel material class. Surface deposition, crystallization, and ion-transport properties remain sample-specific and do not establish identical samples.

clusters.label: Power output
clusters.definition: Electrical energy supplied per unit time by the system.
clusters.reason: Both refer to electrical output power. Salinity-driven diffusion and thermoelectrochemical operation are distinct generating mechanisms, not different power quantities.

clusters.label: Adhesion
clusters.definition: The ability of a material to attach to another surface.
clusters.reason: All describe the same adhesive property without specifying distinct adhesion subtypes or numerical measures; compositions and proposed origins remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Wearable thermoelectric module (PAAM/PDA/CNT-COOH/PANI hydrogel)
clusters.definition: The wearable module fabricated by embedding PAAM/PDA/CNT-COOH/PANI hydrogel in a PDMS mold.
clusters.reason: This denotes a concrete module with an explicit composition and fabrication configuration.

clusters.label: Wearable thermoelectric module (application)
clusters.definition: A wearable thermoelectric module as the intended application of CNT/artificial-biomolecule hybrid yarn.
clusters.reason: This denotes an application target for the specified yarn; the evidence does not identify it with the fabricated hydrogel module.

clusters.label: Charge transport (ionic transport promoted by ionic-electronic interactions)
clusters.definition: Charge transport promoted through sodium-ion interactions with CNT-COOH carboxyl groups, associated with increased ionic conductivity.
clusters.reason: The evidence specifically links this transport to ionic conductivity and ionic-electronic interactions in the hydrogel.

clusters.label: Charge transport (adiabatic small polarons)
clusters.definition: Charge transport described by Mott's adiabatic small-polaron model in Ce/Cr co-doped CaMnO3.
clusters.reason: An explicit small-polaron transport mechanism distinguishes this concept from the hydrogel's ion-related transport.

unresolved.reason: Polymer, nanoparticle, and ionic-liquid interactions improve transport, but the evidence does not identify the carriers or mechanism sufficiently to establish equivalence.

clusters.label: Ion exchange (ionic-liquid-treated PEDOT:PSS)
clusters.definition: Ion exchange induced by ionic-liquid addition or post-treatment in PEDOT:PSS.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify ionic-liquid-induced ion exchange in PEDOT:PSS; differing conductivity and Seebeck consequences do not distinguish the exchange concept. Specific exchanged species are not supplied.

clusters.label: Ion exchange (electrode–geopolymer interface)
clusters.definition: Interfacial ion entry and exit through water microlayers under a temperature gradient, governed by electrode activity and energy-level matching.
clusters.reason: The evidence defines interfacial exchange under thermal driving, distinct from ionic-liquid-induced exchange during PEDOT:PSS treatment.
